pairs.subject: agent-instruction-files
pairs.evidence: scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:388 The dispatch system prompt carries a second, hand-maintained copy of six constitution rules beside the verbatim constitution it appends (line 477), and no test compares that copy with .claude/CLAUDE.md; its 'never touch' list already names fewer paths than PROTECTED_PREFIXES refuses.

techniques.evidence: scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:388 Forked digest of the canonical rules inside an instruction surface, with nothing checking it against the canonical file; dispatch.test.mjs pins the protected set to CI gates but never pins SYSTEM_PROMPT.

scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:228 Tier is decided from author_association, which the workflow gets from the GitHub API and the actor cannot write; a missing value becomes 'none' and is refused (fail closed). The untrusted-label clause (line 410) is backed by this gate, not relied on alone.
scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:291 'Do not edit the gates' is a hard refusal in guardPlan, not prose; injection.test.mjs checks that an obedient model's plan is refused before any file is written.

scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:9 The terminal action (no commit, no push, no merge) is owned in code, not left to a harness default, and lines 33-37 handle the default-GITHUB_TOKEN 'green-by-absence' default explicitly.
scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:474 The constitution and the untrusted label are sent again into each fresh, stateless context instead of assuming round 1's copy survives.
scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:385 The restraints come paired with an outlet (decline with what is missing) and a checkable amplifier: a required 'risks' field (line 512).
scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs:58 The 'patches against unseen paths' failure is fixed by giving the model a capability (a read round), not by adding a steering line.
